name: The Molfar's Path
description: An original tale in the Carpathians: old molfar Yavdokha sends her apprentice with a trembita to Thunder Peak to call the rain.

village.name: Village Below the Mountain
village.text: The hay is dry, the wells are low. Yavdokha puts a trembita on your shoulder: "Go up and ask the Storm."

mill.name: The Water Mill
mill.text: The wheel barely turns. The miller says the river has never been this quiet.

church.name: The Wooden Church
church.text: Shingles silver with age. You light a candle for the road.

beech-forest.name: The Primeval Beeches
beech-forest.text: Grey trunks older than the village. Little green lights drift between them.

vatra.name: Vatra Meadow
vatra.text: The head shepherd gives you an ember from the living fire, wrapped in birch bark.

black-tarn.name: The Black Tarn
black-tarn.text: Water so dark it holds the stars in daylight. You don't drink from it.

stone-guardian.name: The Stone Guardian
stone-guardian.text: An ancient carved stone watches the pass. You bow, and the wind lets you by.

molfar-hut.name: The Old Molfar's Hut
molfar-hut.text: Empty but warm. Dried herbs hang from the beams, as if someone knew you'd come.

seven-winds.name: Pass of Seven Winds
seven-winds.text: Seven winds, seven voices. You answer none of them and keep walking.

thunder-peak.name: Thunder Peak
thunder-peak.text: You blow the trembita. Far to the west, a grey curtain of rain begins to fall over the valley.

story.dust: Dust rises from the road with every step. Even the dogs are too hot to bark.
story.lights: The green lights move ahead of you, always just out of reach. You follow them and don't lose the path.
story.ember: The ember in your pocket stays warm. Yavdokha said it must reach the top alive.
story.clouds-gather: Clouds gather below you, heavy and slow, as if they were waiting for a signal.

facts.molfar: In Hutsul tradition a molfar is a folk healer and weather-maker, believed to be able to turn away hail or call the rain.
facts.tserkvas: In 2013, sixteen wooden churches of the Carpathian region in Poland and Ukraine were added to the UNESCO World Heritage list.
facts.beeches: The Carpathians keep some of Europe's last primeval beech forests; the Ukrainian ones have been World Heritage since 2007.
facts.forest-song: Mavka, a forest spirit of Ukrainian folklore, became the heroine of Lesya Ukrainka's play "The Forest Song" (1911).
facts.vatra-tradition: Shepherds lit the polonyna fire at the start of the grazing season and tried to keep it burning until they drove the flocks down in autumn.
facts.cheese: Budz and brynza, sheep's-milk cheeses, are still made right on the polonyna beside the fire.
facts.shadows: Mykhailo Kotsiubynsky's novella "Shadows of Forgotten Ancestors" (1911) and Serhii Parajanov's 1965 film made Hutsul life known worldwide.
facts.trembita: A trembita is a Hutsul wooden horn that can be over 3 m long. Its call carried news across the valleys: births, weddings, deaths.

ember.name: Keeper of the Ember
ember.description: Get the ember at Vatra Meadow.

rain.name: Rain-Caller
rain.description: Reach Thunder Peak and call the rain.
